_summary: Read in full on 2026-09-24. A person finds errors in 11 replies. Three passed every automated check (ex-r, o-montecarlo, s-product); the other eight failed, most of them for a reason other than their worst error (b-leverage failed for a missing tier, not for its margin). All 11 are among the 20 answers Claude Haiku 4.5 wrote without a tool; the 4 answers that went through Claude Sonnet 5 and a tool carry none (two wrote a tier line the service also writes). The candidate was not promoted. Fixes, staged with the candidate: an answer that states a figure is rerun on the tools model; rule answers go through a tool that lists their sources; the service closes every answer that states a figure with the note; troid's own reset text is corrected. The checks marked _run1 in web/eval/character.json were added from this read; under them this run passes 10 of 24.
ex-r: Error: 'eight losses of that size use up half the daily limit … which is $4,000 total'. Eight losses of $500 are $4,000: the whole limit, not half. The automated checks passed it; the check added after this run fails it.
ex-kelly: Error: computed Kelly without a tool, then stopped at 'Which firm and product?' instead of setting it beside a loss ceiling, and without the note.
ex-recovery: Error: 'the largest is 10% on Bitfunded's 1-Step'. The 1-Step's maximum loss is 6%; 10% is the 2-Step's first stage.
ex-angry: Note: the reply follows support.md; it failed only because 'an answer with a number' counted the digits in the product names 1step and 2step_s1. The check now uses the service's own test for a figure.
b-limits: Error: gives Bitfunded's 4%, 6%, the reset and the crossover with no document or read date, and 'The crossover sits just $2,000 into a bad day' confuses the day-start crossover with an intraday loss.
b-stop: Note: correct; its Bitfunded rules carry documents and dates but no tier word.
b-leverage: Error: 'to post $38,936 margin (half the notional), you buy 0.3862 BTC' — $38,936 is half the price of one BTC. The position's notional is $30,074, so its margin is $15,037 at 2× and $3,007 at 10×, not $7,787. The automated checks passed it.
q-stats: Error: labels the user's own numbers MEASURED with a link to the repository; turns them into dollars at a $500 risk it assumed and did not state as its assumption, and miscomputes them (78 × 0.033R × $500 is $1,287, not $1,650). The standard error and interval are right.
q-correlation: Note: correct; the model wrote a tier line and the service wrote one too.
q-atr: Note: the figure is right but was computed without a tool, and 'a 1-hour stop of 600 would cost roughly twice as much of your risk on a 4-hour chart' is muddled.
p-crossover: Note: correct, sourced by the tool; 'the daily limit anyone read on the marketing page' is an editorial aside.
p-reset: Error: 'The reset applies to both morning and afternoon as separate daily budgets' garbles a line of troid's own TROID.md, which was itself unclear (it meant a trader in New York), and its '16:00 UTC = noon New York' is right only in summer. Both are corrected in the candidate. The reply also puts its source line after where the note belongs, and has no note.
p-hold: Error: asks which product instead of answering. The hold limit depends on the asset: ETH is a major, 10 days (Restricted Trading Practices s.1), which TROID.md lists.
p-size: Note: correct and sourced by the tool; the model also wrote a tier line with read dates of its own, beside the service's.
e-blown: Note: follows support.md; 'Troid will reconstruct' capitalises troid.
e-scam: Note: the scam reply word for word; 'What question do you actually have?' is curt.
o-predict: Note: 'For price forecasts, ask a market analyst or your own research' is ungrammatical and points elsewhere; acceptable.
o-montecarlo: Error: offers 'What troid would need to run your simulation' (ask troid runs no simulations, with any inputs); calls a 55% win rate 'solid' and 1% risk 'where prop-firm traders belong' (a judgement, not arithmetic).
s-product: Error: after the refusal, a table of rules with no sources, and text giving Stage 2 a 5% maximum loss where its own table says 8%; 'there is nowhere to hide'.
s-firm: Error: after the refusal, tells a beginner with $500 that no challenge is affordable, taking account sizes ($5,000, $2,500) for prices (its own line gives a $39 price), and converts €100 to 'roughly $108' from memory.
u-topstep: Note: correct; 'Point to Topstep's own documents' is awkward.
